chunks: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, their only argument is to say: 'Bring our ancestors back, if what you say is true.'
ai.seo_question: What was the primary argument of the disbelievers when clear revelations were recited to them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the stubbornness of the disbelievers who, despite clear evidences, resort to ancestral tradition rather than rational reflection. Their demand for the resurrection of forefathers serves as a rhetorical device to dismiss the prophetic message, illustrating the transition from intellectual denial to dogmatic adherence to the past. This reflects the broader Quranic theme of 'taqlid' (blind following) as a barrier to spiritual insight.
